description: crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:193-196 (commit 9c66783) reads: \"Uses serde_json::Map (which preserves insertion order) rather than HashMap to match the workspace extras-preservation policy and to give callers deterministic serialized output.\" This is FACTUALLY WRONG. `serde_json::Map` is backed by BTreeMap unless the `preserve_order` feature is enabled (it is NOT in this workspace; verified with `cargo tree -e features | grep preserve_order` — no match). BTreeMap iterates in SORTED order, not insertion order. The serialized JSON output IS deterministic — but it is deterministic by lexicographic sort, not by insertion. Trigger: any contributor reading this doc and writing code that relies on insertion-order semantics (e.g. \"the first error I added is rendered first\"). Bad behavior: the rustdoc lies, leading to wrong contributor mental model and to bugs in tests that assume insertion order. Fix: change \"preserves insertion order\" to \"deterministically serializes in lexicographic key order under the workspace's default serde_json features (no preserve_order feature enabled)\". The \"deterministic serialized output\" half of the claim IS correct and should remain. Same false claim is the implicit justification for the HashMap → Map migration in the workspace extras policy text (workspace AGENTS.md line ~370). Audit and correct everywhere.
title: SetError.extra doc-comment falsely claims Map preserves insertion order
